scenarios.title: a new library call in the launch path, no upstream test cited (the lambda incident, 29 Sep)

observations.source: launch note e8 anchor set two + ledger 30 Sep 07:5x
observations.text: The probe smoke with `--fast-t-density` then failed its own pair check at 1.5e-3 a.u. — and the cause was not the kernel: `pyscf.grad.ccsd_t.Gradients(mycc).kernel()` without l1, l2 inherits `ccsd_grad.Gradients.kernel`, which solves `mycc.solve_lambda`, the **CCSD** lambda, and hands it to the (T) density code.

scenarios.title: a record calls a quantity validated without the number and the counterpart (CLAUDE.md, Evidence)

observations.text: six days of CCSD(T) Hessians computed with the CCSD lambda because `Gradients(mycc).kernel()` looked right and its pair checks passed — "Validated" is written only with the number and the counterpart: not "validated on benzene" but "gradient against finite differences of the energy on water, 1e-7". A validation claim without a number counts as not done, and a later reader (including a later session of me) may not build on it.

validation_claim.text: pair checks passed; validated on benzene
